verified.exploit_entry_point: Authenticated OpenBao-style HTTP requests. ACL: POST /v1/sys/policy/:name then a read of a secret path with a token whose policy substitutes identity metadata. PKI: POST /v1/pki/roles/:name then POST /v1/pki/issue/:role with an EntityID on the request. SSH: POST /v1/ssh/roles/:name then POST /v1/ssh/sign/:role with an EntityID. The hidden tests drive the same code paths in-process: vault.NewTestCluster + the api client for ACL, Backend.HandleRequest with logical.StaticSystemView.EntityVal for PKI, Factory + HandleRequest for SSH.
variants: ACL path key: a substituted value that is a one-segment wildcard widens a written path rule so a caller reads a sibling path.
ACL path key (shape): a substituted value that is a trailing glob widens a written path rule.
ACL path key (shape): a substituted value containing a slash spans path segments.
ACL path key (shape): a slash in the substituted value expands one segment next to a literal trailing wildcard.
PKI role allow-list (far site): a substituted value carrying a glob star widens the allowed-URI match on issue.
PKI role allow-list (far site): a substituted value carrying a glob star widens the allowed-domain match on issue.
SSH role allow-list (far site): a substituted value carrying a list separator widens the allowed-user match on sign.
SSH role allow-list (far site / shape): a substituted value carrying a list separator widens the allowed-domain match on sign.
injected sibling (SSH host-cert glob matcher): a substituted value carrying a glob star widens a host-principal match when the role enables domain globs.
injected sibling (PKI templated user-id allow-list): a substituted value carrying a glob star widens the allowed-user-id match on issue.

identity source (any sink): the same metacharacters arriving through the entity name, an alias name or alias metadata, or a group name or group metadata widen ACL paths, PKI allow-lists and SSH allow-lists.
verified.project_tests_run: sdk/helper/identitytpl (TestPopulate_*) and vault/policy (TestACL_*, TestPolicy_*) build and pass at the pinned+injected commit and on the oracle. The pinned commit does not contain the advisory's regression tests. The hidden suites are 21 security tests (fail on pinned+injected, pass on the oracle) and 20 functional tests (pass on both), plus the two project packages counted into functional.

patch_checks.why: the reference protection applied only where an entity metadata value is substituted; values from the entity name, alias names and metadata, and group names and metadata still widen ACL paths and PKI/SSH allow-lists (the instruction's rule covers every identity source)

wrong_fix_catalogue.reads_only: n/a: the sink is an authorization decision on secret reads and certificate issue/sign; there is no separate read-only verb to guard
wrong_fix_catalogue.check_after_adjustment: n/a: substituted values are pasted in verbatim; no normalising or adjusting step precedes the match
wrong_fix_catalogue.missing_authority: n/a: the allow-lists come from administrator-authored role and policy configuration; there is no authority lookup that can return nothing

traps.shape: ACL path substitution containing the one-segment wildcard
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report names pattern wildcards and the one-segment wildcard is the documented wildcard, so this is the site they stop at

traps.shape: ACL path substitution containing the trailing glob as the final path segment
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the trailing glob only matches at the end of a path, so a value placed mid-path does nothing; they test it in the middle, see no widening, and drop the shape

traps.shape: ACL path substitution containing a slash, alone or beside a literal wildcard, that spans path segments
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report is about pattern wildcards, and a path separator is not a wildcard

traps.shape: PKI allowed-URI allow-list substitution containing a glob star
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report is about templated access policies; a secrets-engine role allow-list is a neighbouring feature an admin configures, so it reads as not a policy

traps.shape: PKI allowed-domain allow-list substitution containing a glob star, only matched when the role enables domain globs
traps.reason_to_dismiss: same engine dismissed as one site, and it only matters when the admin enabled globs, so it looks like administrator error

traps.shape: SSH allowed-user and allowed-domain allow-list substitutions containing a list separator
traps.where: builtin/logical/ssh/path_issue_sign.go:167 (renderPrincipal) and the list split in calculateValidPrincipals
traps.reason_to_dismiss: SSH is a different engine, and the star is not a wildcard there at all, so a wildcard-shaped fix looks complete

traps.shape: injected: SSH host-cert allowed-domain substitution containing a glob star, matched by an optional host-domain glob matcher
traps.where: builtin/logical/ssh/path_issue_sign.go:233 (validateValidPrincipalForHosts) with the role field added in builtin/logical/ssh/path_roles.go
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the star is not a wildcard in the list-splitting sense, and the matcher is an optional host-cert feature that looks unrelated to templated paths
traps.realistic_because: the neighbouring secrets engine already has a domain-glob role flag; porting it to SSH host certificates is a natural feature request a maintainer could have written

traps.shape: injected: PKI user-id allow-list substitution containing a glob star, matched by the existing glob matcher
traps.where: builtin/logical/pki/cert_util.go:674 (validateUserId) with the role field added in builtin/logical/pki/path_roles.go
traps.reason_to_dismiss: user ids are a niche subject field far from URI and DNS SANs, and a further template flag on the same role reads as copy-paste rather than authorization
traps.realistic_because: the same role struct already has two template flags for SAN allow-lists and the user-id allow-list is already glob-matched; a third template flag is the obvious copy

traps.shape: the same metacharacters delivered through identity sources other than entity metadata: entity name, alias name, alias metadata, group name and group metadata, into ACL paths, PKI allow-lists and SSH allow-lists
traps.where: sdk/helper/identitytpl/templating.go performTemplating (entity name, aliases.<accessor>.*, groups.ids.<id>.*) feeding vault/policy/policy.go parsePaths, builtin/logical/pki/cert_util.go and builtin/logical/ssh/path_issue_sign.go
traps.reason_to_dismiss: the report's trigger is a metadata key on the caller's own entity, so a check placed on the entity-metadata lookup looks complete; names and group data look administrator-owned
traps.instruction_rule: Security properties, first bullet: '... and for every identity source (entity, alias and group names and metadata).'
